buttons.create.summary: Places an action button on a sheet; a click runs a script from the library, or one of its functions. Returns the identifier of the button.
buttons.create.details: script is the name of a saved script (Script tab). With function, the script is loaded, then the global function of that name is called: one script can serve several buttons. Everything a click does is undone at once. Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; label: text of the button; script: name of the script to run; function: function of the script to call; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: buttons.create{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

buttons.delete.details: Parameters — button: button (identifier or label). Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

buttons.list.signature: buttons.list([sheet]) → { {id, name, kind, label, script, function, row, col}, ... }
buttons.list.summary: Lists the action buttons of a sheet.
buttons.list.details: Parameters — sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet.

buttons.place.summary: Moves a button (top-left corner at row, col) and, if given, resizes it (pixels).
buttons.place.details: Parameters — button: button (identifier or label); row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; width: width in pixels; height: height in pixels. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: buttons.place{button = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

buttons.set.summary: Changes the label, the script or the function of a button (missing parameters do not change).
buttons.set.details: Parameters — button: button (identifier or label); label: text of the button; script: name of the script; function: function of the script ("": the script alone). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: buttons.set{button = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.clear.summary: Clears the content of a range of cells (tables keep their shape).
cells.clear.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; row2: last row of the range (missing: row); col2: last column of the range (missing: col); sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.clear{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.dependencies.summary: Gives the precedents (what the cell's formula reads) and the dependents (the formulas that read it).
cells.dependencies.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.dependencies{row = …}.

cells.get.signature: cells.get(row, col, [sheet]) → {row, col, raw, value, table, column, header, line, id}
cells.get.summary: Reads a cell of the sheet: entry, displayed value and, in a table, the table, the column and the row.
cells.get.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.get{row = …}.

cells.goal_seek.summary: Goal seek: looks for the value of the cell changing (a constant, or a typed cell of a table) for which the formula of the cell target equals value, and sets it (unless keep = false).
cells.goal_seek.details: Secant, then bracketing and Brent's method (300 evaluations at most). found is false when no value gives exactly value: value is then the closest one found, set only if keep = true is given. Parameters — target: cell to set, with a formula ("B5"); value: value to reach; changing: cell to change ("B1"); keep: false: only search, without changing anything; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.goal_seek{target = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.merge.signature: cells.merge(row, col, [row2], [col2], [sheet]) → number of values cleared
cells.merge.summary: Merges free cells into one, with centered content (refused in a table or a PivotTable). Like Excel, only the top-left value is kept. In a table with header groups (tables.two_level_headers), only the group band merges: its box and the header of a column put the column on one level (simple name: its subheader, or the group if the header was automatic); several neighboring boxes of the band form a single group (the first one they carry, “Group” otherwise). Columns are renamed, formulas follow.
cells.merge.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; row2: last row of the range (missing: row); col2: last column of the range (missing: col); sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.merge{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.name.summary: Names a free cell, to cite it in formulas; an empty name removes the name.
cells.name.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; name: name (empty: remove); sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.name{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.note.summary: Sets the note of a cell (red corner, shown on hover); an empty text removes it. In a table, the note follows its row.
cells.note.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; text: text of the note (empty: remove it); sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.note{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.paste.summary: Writes a block of values from a cell, like a paste: a row of headers followed by rows of data creates a table; range = true writes it as a range of free cells.
cells.paste.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; values: rows of values: { {"Name", "Age"}, {"Lea", 31} }; range: true: free cells (a range), without creating a table; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.paste{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.read.summary: Reads the displayed values of a range of the sheet, row by row: tables, PivotTables and free cells alike ("": empty cell).
cells.read.details: 100,000 cells at most; for a whole table, tables.rows or db.query are more direct. Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; row2: last row of the range; col2: last column of the range; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.read{row = …}.

cells.set.signature: cells.set(row, col, value, [sheet]) → {created, widened, from, to, invalid, keyed}
cells.set.summary: Enters a value in a cell of the sheet, exactly like typing in the grid.
cells.set.details: A text that starts with = is a formula. Typing next to a table extends it, typing two adjacent rows creates a table, "" clears the cell. Returns what the entry caused (table created, column widened…). Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; value: entry: text, number, boolean, formula (=…); sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.set{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.style.details: style: bold, italic, underline, strike (booleans), font (font name) and size (size in points), color and fill (colors "#rrggbb", or from the workbook theme: "theme:accent1" to "theme:accent6", "theme:dk1", "theme:lt1", "theme:dk2", "theme:lt2", followed if needed by ":+40" for 40% lighter or ":-25" for 25% darker; they change with the theme), align ("left", "center" or "right"), valign ("top", "middle" or "bottom"), wrap (wrap text), format ("0", "0,00", "%", "€", "date", "time" or "text"), decimals (number of decimal places), no_grouping (no thousands separator), date_format (pattern of a date or a time: "jj/mm/aaaa", "jj mmm aaaa", "aaaa-mm-jj", "hh:mm"…), format_code (custom number format code: '# ##0.00 "kg"', "0.00E+00", "# ?/?", "0;[Red]-0"; overrides format), borders (all four borders) or border_top, border_bottom, border_left, border_right, border_color (default color; an edge is true for a thin line, or "style color": "thin", "medium", "thick", "double", "dotted" or "dashed", followed if needed by a color: "double #c00000"), and validation (drop-down list: list of allowed values {"Yes", "No"}, or source range "=Customers[City]", "=Cell[A1:A10]", "=Sheet2!Cell[A1:A10]" or "=CellName", whose distinct non-blank values are read again each time the list opens and at each entry; or a rule {type = "whole", op = "between", min = 1, max = 10}: type "whole", "decimal", "date", "time", "length", "list" (with list or src), "custom" (formula = "=ISNUMBER(B2)", written for the cell at = "B2") or "any", op "between", "notbetween", "=", "<>", ">", "<", ">=" or "<=", min and max (value or formula "=B1"), blank = false (blank refused), input = {title, msg} (input message), error = {style = "stop", "warning" or "info", title, msg} (alert); checked when typing in the grid, not for scripts). false or "" removes the property. link (hyperlink: "https://…", "mailto:…", or "#Sheet2!B3", "#B3", "#Table"; other schemes are refused; the cell value stays the text shown). Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; row2: last row of the range (missing: row); col2: last column of the range (missing: col); style: properties to set: {bold = true, fill = "#fff2cc"}; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.style{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.style_lines.summary: Formats whole rows or columns of the sheet (all their cells, present and future, tables and PivotTables included). A cell takes precedence over its row, a row over its column.
cells.style_lines.details: style: bold, italic, underline, strike (booleans), font (font name) and size (size in points), color and fill (colors "#rrggbb", or from the workbook theme: "theme:accent1" to "theme:accent6", "theme:dk1", "theme:lt1", "theme:dk2", "theme:lt2", followed if needed by ":+40" for 40% lighter or ":-25" for 25% darker; they change with the theme), align ("left", "center" or "right"), valign ("top", "middle" or "bottom"), wrap (wrap text), format ("0", "0,00", "%", "€", "date", "time" or "text"), decimals (number of decimal places), no_grouping (no thousands separator), date_format (pattern of a date or a time: "jj/mm/aaaa", "jj mmm aaaa", "aaaa-mm-jj", "hh:mm"…), format_code (custom number format code: '# ##0.00 "kg"', "0.00E+00", "# ?/?", "0;[Red]-0"; overrides format), borders (all four borders) or border_top, border_bottom, border_left, border_right, border_color (default color; an edge is true for a thin line, or "style color": "thin", "medium", "thick", "double", "dotted" or "dashed", followed if needed by a color: "double #c00000"), and validation (drop-down list: list of allowed values {"Yes", "No"}, or source range "=Customers[City]", "=Cell[A1:A10]", "=Sheet2!Cell[A1:A10]" or "=CellName", whose distinct non-blank values are read again each time the list opens and at each entry; or a rule {type = "whole", op = "between", min = 1, max = 10}: type "whole", "decimal", "date", "time", "length", "list" (with list or src), "custom" (formula = "=ISNUMBER(B2)", written for the cell at = "B2") or "any", op "between", "notbetween", "=", "<>", ">", "<", ">=" or "<=", min and max (value or formula "=B1"), blank = false (blank refused), input = {title, msg} (input message), error = {style = "stop", "warning" or "info", title, msg} (alert); checked when typing in the grid, not for scripts). false or "" removes the property. Parameters — axis: "rows" or "cols" (columns); from: first row or column, from 1; to: last row or column (missing: from); style: properties to set: {bold = true, fill = "#fff2cc"}; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.style_lines{axis = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.text_to_columns.summary: Splits the text of the cells of column col, rows row to row2, into columns (Excel's Text to Columns wizard): in free cells, the parts are written to the right (or from options.dest); in a table, new columns are inserted. Returns the number of columns imported.
cells.text_to_columns.details: options: {delims, merge, quote, fixed, breaks, columns, decimal, thousands, dest}. delims: separator characters (";", ",", " ", "	"…); merge = true: consecutive separators count as one; quote: text qualifier ("\"" by default in the wizard, "'" or "" for none). fixed = true: fixed width, breaks gives the positions of the breaks (in characters). columns: format of each column produced, {format = "" (general), "text", "date" or "skip" (not imported), order = "DMY", "MDY", "YMD"… for dates}. decimal and thousands: number separators ("," and " " by default). dest: destination cell (“E2”) in free cells. Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; row2: last row of the range (missing: row); options: {delims, merge, quote, fixed, breaks, columns, decimal, thousands, dest}; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.text_to_columns{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.to_values.summary: Replaces the formulas of a range with their values: free cells with a formula, and calculated columns (whole) of the tables the range touches (like columns.to_values). Formulas that spill a dynamic array are kept.
cells.to_values.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; row2: last row of the range (missing: row); col2: last column of the range (missing: col); sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.to_values{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

cells.unmerge.summary: Undoes the merges of cells that touch the range. In the header group band of a table, a group over several columns stays on the first, the others go to one level (renamed); a column on one level does not change: give it a group with cells.set on the band or columns.rename(“Group.Sub”).
cells.unmerge.details: Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; row2: last row of the range (missing: row); col2: last column of the range (missing: col); sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: cells.unmerge{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

charts.create.summary: Places a chart on a sheet, top-left corner at row, col, and returns its identifier.
charts.create.details:
config: {source, kind, x, series, title, …}. source is a table or a PivotTable, x the column of the categories (x axis), series the list of plotted columns. kind: "bar" (column chart: vertical bars), "column" (horizontal bars), "line", "area", "pie", "doughnut", "scatter", "combo" (bars and lines: seriesKinds gives the shape of each series, "bar", "line" or "area"), "bar3d" and "pie3d" (in perspective), "map" (OpenStreetMap map), "waterfall", "treemap", "radar", "funnel", "boxplot" (box and whisker), "histogram" (frequencies, bins classes), "gauge" (last value of the first series, between yMin and yMax), "bubble" (x numeric, series in pairs {Y, size}) or "stock" (series = {high, low, close} or {open, high, low, close, optional volume}, one candle per row).
Layout: title; legend ("bottom", "top", "right" or "none"); xTitle, yTitle, y2Title (axis titles); labels (data labels); noGrid (no gridlines); stacked (bars, areas); yMin, yMax (bounds of the value axis); colors (color of each series, "#rrggbb"; per category for pie, doughnut, funnel and treemap; increase, decrease and total for the waterfall); secondary (list of booleans: series on the right axis); blanks (lines and areas: blank cell "gap" as a gap, the default, "zero" or "span" to connect the points); hidden (also reads the rows hidden by the table filter); filters (chart drawn from a table: {{field, values}, ...}, reads only the rows whose field column shows one of the values, like the report filter of a PivotTable; on the column of a choice tab, it takes precedence over the choice); width, height (pixels) and offX, offY (offset within the anchor cell, pixels).
Map: series = {latitude, longitude, optional value} (mapCoords "pair", the default) or {coordinates, optional value} (mapCoords "single": one cell “48.85, 2.35”); x the name of the points; mapMode "points", "heat" (density) or "both" (the two together); colorBy, column whose each value gets its own color; mapScale, size factor of the points (1 by default, from 0.25 to 4); mapView {lat, lon, zoom} sets the view.
Analysis (bars, lines, areas, scatter, combo, bubbles; not stacked): trendlines, trendline of each series by rank ({ {type = "linear"}, nil, … }): type "linear", "exp", "log", "poly" (order from 2 to 6), "power" or "movavg" (moving average, period from 2 to 255); forward, backward: forecast after and before (units of X, categories on a category axis); equation, r2: shown on the chart. errorBars, error bars of each series by rank: type "fixed" (value), "percent" (value %), "stddev" (value standard deviations, 1 by default, around the mean), "stderr" (standard error) or "custom" (amounts from the plus and minus columns; minus missing: those of plus); dir "both" (default), "plus" or "minus"; noCap: without end caps. Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; config: configuration of the chart; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: charts.create{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

charts.delete.details: Parameters — chart: chart (identifier or title). Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

charts.place.summary: Moves a chart (top-left corner at row, col) and, if given, resizes it (pixels, at least 160 × 120); otherwise it keeps its size.
charts.place.details: Parameters — chart: chart (identifier or title); row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; width: width in pixels; height: height in pixels. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: charts.place{chart = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

charts.set.summary: Changes the configuration of a chart: only the given fields change (replace = true replaces the whole configuration).
charts.set.details:
config: {source, kind, x, series, title, …}. source is a table or a PivotTable, x the column of the categories (x axis), series the list of plotted columns. kind: "bar" (column chart: vertical bars), "column" (horizontal bars), "line", "area", "pie", "doughnut", "scatter", "combo" (bars and lines: seriesKinds gives the shape of each series, "bar", "line" or "area"), "bar3d" and "pie3d" (in perspective), "map" (OpenStreetMap map), "waterfall", "treemap", "radar", "funnel", "boxplot" (box and whisker), "histogram" (frequencies, bins classes), "gauge" (last value of the first series, between yMin and yMax), "bubble" (x numeric, series in pairs {Y, size}) or "stock" (series = {high, low, close} or {open, high, low, close, optional volume}, one candle per row).
Layout: title; legend ("bottom", "top", "right" or "none"); xTitle, yTitle, y2Title (axis titles); labels (data labels); noGrid (no gridlines); stacked (bars, areas); yMin, yMax (bounds of the value axis); colors (color of each series, "#rrggbb"; per category for pie, doughnut, funnel and treemap; increase, decrease and total for the waterfall); secondary (list of booleans: series on the right axis); blanks (lines and areas: blank cell "gap" as a gap, the default, "zero" or "span" to connect the points); hidden (also reads the rows hidden by the table filter); filters (chart drawn from a table: {{field, values}, ...}, reads only the rows whose field column shows one of the values, like the report filter of a PivotTable; on the column of a choice tab, it takes precedence over the choice); width, height (pixels) and offX, offY (offset within the anchor cell, pixels).
Map: series = {latitude, longitude, optional value} (mapCoords "pair", the default) or {coordinates, optional value} (mapCoords "single": one cell “48.85, 2.35”); x the name of the points; mapMode "points", "heat" (density) or "both" (the two together); colorBy, column whose each value gets its own color; mapScale, size factor of the points (1 by default, from 0.25 to 4); mapView {lat, lon, zoom} sets the view.
Analysis (bars, lines, areas, scatter, combo, bubbles; not stacked): trendlines, trendline of each series by rank ({ {type = "linear"}, nil, … }): type "linear", "exp", "log", "poly" (order from 2 to 6), "power" or "movavg" (moving average, period from 2 to 255); forward, backward: forecast after and before (units of X, categories on a category axis); equation, r2: shown on the chart. errorBars, error bars of each series by rank: type "fixed" (value), "percent" (value %), "stddev" (value standard deviations, 1 by default, around the mean), "stderr" (standard error) or "custom" (amounts from the plus and minus columns; minus missing: those of plus); dir "both" (default), "plus" or "minus"; noCap: without end caps. Parameters — chart: chart (identifier or title); config: fields to change; replace: replace the whole configuration (size, colors, map view… go back to default). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: charts.set{chart = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.delete.summary: Deletes a column of a table (a table keeps at least one column).
columns.delete.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.delete{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.fix_type.summary: Fixes the current type of a column: it will no longer widen, an entry outside the type will be marked as an error.
columns.fix_type.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.fix_type{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.insert.summary: Inserts a column in a table, before column position (missing: at the end).
columns.insert.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; name: name of the column; position: position, from 1. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.insert{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.rename.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1); name: new name. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.rename{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.set_filter.summary: Filters a table on a column: only the rows whose value is in values stay displayed.
columns.set_filter.details: values is a list of texts as displayed ("" for empty cells); errors = true keeps only the entries in error. conds filters by condition, like Excel's “Text Filters” and “Number Filters”: each condition is {op, value, to} with op among "eq", "ne" (wildcards * and ?), "begins", "ends", "contains", "notcontains", "gt", "ge", "lt", "le", "between" (value and to included), "top" and "bottom" (value: number of items), "above" and "below" (average). The conditions must all be met, or one of them with any = true. Without values, errors or conds, the filter of the column is removed. Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1); values: values kept; errors: keep only the errors; conds: conditions: { {op = ">", value = "100"}, ... }; any: a single condition is enough. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.set_filter{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.set_rules.summary: Replaces the conditional formatting rules of a column (empty list: none); the first rule met wins.
columns.set_rules.details: Each rule is {op, value, to, style}. op: ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "=", "<>", "between" (between value and to), "contains", "empty", "notempty" or "error". style: bold, italic, underline, strike (booleans), font (font name) and size (size in points), color and fill (colors "#rrggbb", or from the workbook theme: "theme:accent1" to "theme:accent6", "theme:dk1", "theme:lt1", "theme:dk2", "theme:lt2", followed if needed by ":+40" for 40% lighter or ":-25" for 25% darker; they change with the theme), align ("left", "center" or "right"), valign ("top", "middle" or "bottom"), wrap (wrap text), format ("0", "0,00", "%", "€", "date", "time" or "text"), decimals (number of decimal places), no_grouping (no thousands separator), date_format (pattern of a date or a time: "jj/mm/aaaa", "jj mmm aaaa", "aaaa-mm-jj", "hh:mm"…), format_code (custom number format code: '# ##0.00 "kg"', "0.00E+00", "# ?/?", "0;[Red]-0"; overrides format), borders (all four borders) or border_top, border_bottom, border_left, border_right, border_color (default color; an edge is true for a thin line, or "style color": "thin", "medium", "thick", "double", "dotted" or "dashed", followed if needed by a color: "double #c00000"), and validation (drop-down list: list of allowed values {"Yes", "No"}, or source range "=Customers[City]", "=Cell[A1:A10]", "=Sheet2!Cell[A1:A10]" or "=CellName", whose distinct non-blank values are read again each time the list opens and at each entry; or a rule {type = "whole", op = "between", min = 1, max = 10}: type "whole", "decimal", "date", "time", "length", "list" (with list or src), "custom" (formula = "=ISNUMBER(B2)", written for the cell at = "B2") or "any", op "between", "notbetween", "=", "<>", ">", "<", ">=" or "<=", min and max (value or formula "=B1"), blank = false (blank refused), input = {title, msg} (input message), error = {style = "stop", "warning" or "info", title, msg} (alert); checked when typing in the grid, not for scripts). false or "" removes the property. Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1); rules: rules: { {op = ">", value = "100", style = {fill = "#c6efce"}}, ... }. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.set_rules{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.set_type.summary: Sets the type of a column; values that do not convert stay visible, marked as errors.
columns.set_type.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1); type: integer, decimal, text, boolean or date. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.set_type{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.sort_order.signature: columns.sort_order(table, column) → {list, values = {...}, desc, applied}: applied if it is the last sort of the table
columns.sort_order.summary: Returns the saved custom order of a column (nil: none).
columns.sort_order.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.sort_order{table = …}.

columns.to_values.summary: Turns a calculated column into a typed column that keeps its current values, with the type guessed from these values. It keeps its name (formulas that cite it still read it) but no longer follows the sources of its formula. Refused in a shared table of a collaborative workbook.
columns.to_values.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.to_values{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

columns.type_mix.summary: For a column turned into text by widening: majority type and number of values that are not of it.

columns.type_preview.summary: Counts the values of a column that would not convert to the given type.
columns.type_preview.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1); type: integer, decimal, text, boolean or date. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.type_preview{table = …}.

columns.values.summary: Lists the distinct values of a column with their number of occurrences (1,000 at most).
columns.values.details: Parameters — table: name of the table; column: column (name or position from 1). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: columns.values{table = …}.

controls.add.signature: controls.add(kind, row, col, [props], [sheet]) → {id, name, kind, …} (like controls.get)
controls.add.summary: Places a control on a sheet, top-left corner at row, col, and returns it described (its name is chosen automatically if not given).
controls.add.details: A control has a name that is unique in the workbook (“Button1”, “List1”…), chosen automatically and editable. kind: "button" (a click runs its action), "checkbox" (TRUE / FALSE), "select" (drop-down list, options), "input" (single-line text), "textarea" (multi-line text) or "file" (file picker: the cell receives the path of the chosen file). Except for the button, a control is linked to a cell (link, “B3”): its value (value) is that cell's — a boolean for a checkbox, a text otherwise. Properties: name, label (text of the button or the checkbox, placeholder of an input box), link, value (written to the linked cell; fires the change event if it changes), options (drop-down list), script and function (action of the control), color, hoverColor, activeColor, textColor (“#rrggbb”), hidden or visible, row, col, width, height (pixels). Without link, a control other than a button is linked to the cell on its right. Parameters — kind: "button", "checkbox", "select", "input", "textarea" or "file"; row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; props: properties: {label = …, link = "B3" (optional: without a linked cell, the value is kept in the control), options = {…} or optionsFrom = "Customers[City]" (choices taken from a column), …}; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: controls.add{kind = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

controls.delete.summary: Deletes a control (its linked cell keeps its value).
controls.delete.details: Parameters — control: control (name, identifier or label). Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

controls.fire.signature: controls.fire(control, [event]) → {output, writes, durationMs, error} (outside a script)
controls.fire.summary: Fires an event of a control like the interface does (click of a button, change with the current value of the others): its action, then its listeners, run.

Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

controls.get.signature: controls.get(control) → {id, name, kind, label, sheet, row, col, width, height, link, value, options, script, function, color, hoverColor, activeColor, textColor, hidden, listeners}
controls.get.summary: Describes a control: kind, label, linked cell and its value, choices, colors, position, action and listeners.

controls.list.summary: Lists the controls (buttons, checkboxes, lists, input boxes, file pickers) of a sheet, or of the whole workbook.
controls.list.details: A control has a name that is unique in the workbook (“Button1”, “List1”…), chosen automatically and editable. kind: "button" (a click runs its action), "checkbox" (TRUE / FALSE), "select" (drop-down list, options), "input" (single-line text), "textarea" (multi-line text) or "file" (file picker: the cell receives the path of the chosen file). Except for the button, a control is linked to a cell (link, “B3”): its value (value) is that cell's — a boolean for a checkbox, a text otherwise. Parameters — sheet: sheet (missing: the whole workbook).

controls.listeners.summary: Lists what the events of a control, or of all of them, run: its action (action = true), then its listeners, in order.
controls.listeners.details: Events: "click" (button) and "change" (new value of the other controls, entry in the sheet or controls.set). A listener is a global function of a script saved in the library, called with the table {control, event, value, old} (also in the global variable event); it is saved in the workbook and outlives the script. The action of the control (script and function) runs first, then the listeners in order. Events caused by a script run when it ends, in the same undo step. Parameters — control: control (missing: all).

controls.off.summary: Unsubscribes listeners of a control and returns their number: all, or those of an event, a function, a script.
controls.off.details: The action of the control (script and function, Edit window) is not a listener: controls.set(name, {script = ""}) removes it. Parameters — control: control (name, identifier or label); event: event (missing: all); handler: function (or its name; missing: all); script: script (missing: all). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: controls.off{control = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

controls.on.summary: Subscribes a function of a script to an event of a control ("click" of a button, "change" of the others); it will be called at each event with {control, event, value, old}.
controls.on.details: Events: "click" (button) and "change" (new value of the other controls, entry in the sheet or controls.set). A listener is a global function of a script saved in the library, called with the table {control, event, value, old} (also in the global variable event); it is saved in the workbook and outlives the script. The action of the control (script and function) runs first, then the listeners in order. Events caused by a script run when it ends, in the same undo step. handler is the function itself or its name; script, by default the running script (it must be saved in the library). Subscribing the same function twice changes nothing. Parameters — control: control (name, identifier or label); event: "click" or "change"; handler: global function of the script (or its name); script: script of the function (missing: the running script). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: controls.on{control = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

controls.set.summary: Changes properties of a control (the others do not change): label, value, choices, colors, visibility, position.
controls.set.details: Properties: name, label (text of the button or the checkbox, placeholder of an input box), link, value (written to the linked cell; fires the change event if it changes), options (drop-down list), script and function (action of the control), color, hoverColor, activeColor, textColor (“#rrggbb”), hidden or visible, row, col, width, height (pixels). Writing value amounts to entering the value in the linked cell. Parameters — control: control (name, identifier or label); props: properties to change: {value = …, hidden = true, …}. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: controls.set{control = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

doc.recalc.details: Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

doc.set_theme.summary: Changes the color theme of the workbook: two base colors #rrggbb, the shades (header, text, border) are derived from them. Without colors: the default theme of the settings.
doc.set_theme.details: Parameters — table: color of ordinary tables, #rrggbb; source: color of the tables of an external source (query), #rrggbb; name: name of the theme. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: doc.set_theme{table = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

doc.state.signature: doc.state() → {open, path, title, dirty, undo, redo}
doc.state.summary: Describes the open workbook: file, unsaved changes, actions to undo and redo.

doc.theme.signature: doc.theme() → {id, name, table, source} or nil
doc.theme.summary: Color theme of the workbook (View › Theme): color of ordinary tables (table) and of the tables of an external source (source). nil: default theme of the settings.

events.enable.signature: events.enable(on) → true if the events were on
events.enable.summary: Turns the workbook events on (true) or off (false) for the session, like Excel's Application.EnableEvents; returns the previous state.
events.enable.details: When off, no listener of the workbook events runs; the events of the controls (controls.on) are not affected. Opening a workbook turns them back on. Parameters — on: true: turn on; false: turn off.

events.enabled.summary: Says whether the workbook events are on (events.enable).

events.list.summary: Lists the listeners of the workbook events, in the order they run.
events.list.details: Events: "open" (workbook opened: {path, title}); "before_save" (before saving (Ctrl+S, Save As): {path, as}; returning false cancels it); "save" (after saving: {path}); "before_close" (before closing the workbook or the window: {path, dirty}; returning false cancels it); "sheet" (displayed tab changed: {sheet, sheet_id, previous, previous_id}); "selection" (selection changed, once the mouse or keyboard is idle: {sheet, sheet_id, row, col, row2, col2, address, table, column}); "change" (cells changed by the user (entry, paste, clear, move, table row added or deleted): {sheet, sheet_id, row, col, row2, col2, address, table, column, value, old, source}); "sheet_add" (sheet added (or copied): {sheet, sheet_id}); "sheet_delete" (sheet deleted: {sheet, sheet_id}); "recalc" (formulas recalculated (F9, Recalculate): {}). Each table also carries event (the name of the event); rows and columns count from 1, like ui.selection. value and old (displayed value after and before) are given only for a single cell entered. Only the user's actions fire these events: what a script (listener included) changes, selects or displays fires none, so a listener never triggers itself. A listener is a global function of a script saved in the library, called with the table of the event (also in the global variable event); it is saved in the workbook and outlives the script. events.off.summary: Unsubscribes listeners of the workbook events and returns their number: all, or those of an event, a function, a script.
events.off.details: Parameters — event: event (missing: all); handler: function (or its name; missing: all); script: script (missing: all). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: events.off{event = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

events.on.details: Events: "open" (workbook opened: {path, title}); "before_save" (before saving (Ctrl+S, Save As): {path, as}; returning false cancels it); "save" (after saving: {path}); "before_close" (before closing the workbook or the window: {path, dirty}; returning false cancels it); "sheet" (displayed tab changed: {sheet, sheet_id, previous, previous_id}); "selection" (selection changed, once the mouse or keyboard is idle: {sheet, sheet_id, row, col, row2, col2, address, table, column}); "change" (cells changed by the user (entry, paste, clear, move, table row added or deleted): {sheet, sheet_id, row, col, row2, col2, address, table, column, value, old, source}); "sheet_add" (sheet added (or copied): {sheet, sheet_id}); "sheet_delete" (sheet deleted: {sheet, sheet_id}); "recalc" (formulas recalculated (F9, Recalculate): {}). Each table also carries event (the name of the event); rows and columns count from 1, like ui.selection. value and old (displayed value after and before) are given only for a single cell entered. Subscribing the same function twice changes nothing. Parameters — event: "open", "before_save", "save", "before_close", "sheet", "selection", "change", "sheet_add", "sheet_delete" or "recalc"; handler: global function of the script (or its name); script: script of the function (missing: the running script). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: events.on{event = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

http.get.signature: http.get(url, [options]) → {status, ok, url, headers, body, json}
http.get.summary: Sends an HTTP GET request (http:// or https://) and returns the response.
http.get.details: The response: status (200, 404…), ok (true for a 2xx status), url (final address, after redirects), headers (lowercase names), body (text) and json (the decoded body when the response is JSON). An error status (404, 500…) is not a Lua error: test ok; a network failure or a timeout is one (use pcall to catch it). Before the first request to a host, Lattis asks the user for permission (can be remembered for the workbook; Script tab › Network access to review it); the MCP server only reaches hosts already allowed. Timeout: 15 s by default (timeout, 120 s at most), not counted in the maximum duration of the script; response of 10 MB at most; 10 redirects at most; the Stop button interrupts the request. Parameters — url: address (http:// or https://); options: {headers = {name = value}, timeout = seconds}. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: http.get{url = …}.

http.post.signature: http.post(url, [body], [options]) → {status, ok, url, headers, body, json}
http.post.summary: Sends an HTTP POST request and returns the response; a text body is sent as is, a table is sent as JSON.
http.post.details: The response: status (200, 404…), ok (true for a 2xx status), url (final address, after redirects), headers (lowercase names), body (text) and json (the decoded body when the response is JSON). An error status (404, 500…) is not a Lua error: test ok; a network failure or a timeout is one (use pcall to catch it). Before the first request to a host, Lattis asks the user for permission (can be remembered for the workbook; Script tab › Network access to review it); the MCP server only reaches hosts already allowed. Timeout: 15 s by default (timeout, 120 s at most), not counted in the maximum duration of the script; response of 10 MB at most; 10 redirects at most; the Stop button interrupts the request. Parameters — url: address (http:// or https://); body: body: text, or table encoded as JSON (Content-Type: application/json); options: {headers = {name = value}, timeout = seconds}. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: http.post{url = …}.

http.request.signature: http.request(url, [method], [headers], [body], [json], [timeout]) → {status, ok, url, headers, body, json}
http.request.summary: Sends any HTTP request (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE…) and returns the response.
http.request.details: json encodes a table as a JSON body (with the matching Content-Type header); body sends a text as is. The response: status (200, 404…), ok (true for a 2xx status), url (final address, after redirects), headers (lowercase names), body (text) and json (the decoded body when the response is JSON). An error status (404, 500…) is not a Lua error: test ok; a network failure or a timeout is one (use pcall to catch it). Before the first request to a host, Lattis asks the user for permission (can be remembered for the workbook; Script tab › Network access to review it); the MCP server only reaches hosts already allowed. Timeout: 15 s by default (timeout, 120 s at most), not counted in the maximum duration of the script; response of 10 MB at most; 10 redirects at most; the Stop button interrupts the request. Parameters — url: address (http:// or https://); method: method (GET by default); headers: headers: {name = value}; body: body of the request (text); json: body of the request: table encoded as JSON; timeout: timeout in seconds (15 by default, 120 at most). Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: http.request{url = …}.

objects.create.summary: Places a shape, a text box or an image on a sheet, top-left corner at row, col, and returns its identifier.
objects.create.details: config: {kind, width, height, offX, offY, name, fill, line, lineWidth, transparency, text, bold, italic, size, color, align, valign, flipH, flipV, data, image}. kind: "rect", "roundRect" (rounded rectangle), "ellipse", "triangle", "line", "arrow", "text" (text box) or "image". width, height: size in pixels (by default according to the kind; an image keeps its proportions, 480 pixels wide at most); offX, offY: offset within the anchor cell. fill and line: colors of the fill and the outline ("#rrggbb", "": none); lineWidth: width of the outline (pixels); transparency: transparency of the fill (0 to 100). text: text of the shape or the text box, formatted by bold, italic, size (points), color, align ("left", "center", "right") and valign ("top", "middle", "bottom"). flipH, flipV: direction of a line or an arrow (by default from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner, the head at the end). An image is given by data (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP content in base64, 10 MB at most) or by image (hash of an image already in the workbook, see objects.list). Parameters — row: sheet row, from 1; col: sheet column, from 1; config: kind and formatting of the object; sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: objects.create{row = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

objects.delete.summary: Deletes an image, a shape or a text box.
objects.delete.details: Parameters — object: object (identifier or name). Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

objects.list.signature: objects.list([sheet]) → { {id, kind, name, row, col, offX, offY, width, height, text, image}, ... }
objects.list.summary: Lists the images, shapes and text boxes of a sheet, from the back to the front.
objects.list.details: Parameters — sheet: sheet (name or identifier); missing: the displayed sheet.

pages.add.summary: Adds a web page (HTML, CSS and JavaScript displayed in an isolated frame), or a document (kind = "doc": rich text), and returns {id, name, kind}.
pages.add.details: The page talks to the workbook with lattis.call("command", {arguments}), which returns a promise (an allowed list of the script commands: reading like sheets.list or db.query, values like cells.set or db.execute, ui.*, http.*, buttons.run; no files, no scripts, no structure, no protections), and lattis.on("change", function), called when the workbook changes. It also reads the workbook with lattis.sql("SELECT …", {parameters}) and lattis.query("name of a saved query"), which return an array of objects. Web pages are off by default (features.htmlPages configuration setting, never in the browser edition); documents (kind = "doc") remain allowed. Without source, the page receives a sample template. Without before, the tab is added at the end. Parameters — name: name of the tab (Page1… by default); source: HTML content of the page; before: sheet before which to insert it; kind: "html" (default) or "doc": document, whose content is a Quill Delta in JSON. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: pages.add{name = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

pages.get.summary: Returns the HTML content of a web page.
pages.get.details: Parameters — sheet: web page (name or identifier); missing: the displayed tab.

pages.set.summary: Replaces the HTML content of a web page.
pages.set.details: Web pages are off by default (features.htmlPages configuration setting). Parameters — sheet: web page (name or identifier); source: new HTML content. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: pages.set{sheet = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

pivots.create.summary: Creates a PivotTable on a new sheet and returns that sheet.
pivots.create.details: config: {source, rowFields, cols, values, filters, calc, name, noGrandTotal, subtotals, collapsed, collapseAll, expanded}. source is a table, rowFields the list of row fields, cols the column field, values a list of {field, agg, show} (agg: "sum", "count", "countDistinct", "avg", "min" or "max"; show: "", "pctTotal", "pctRow" or "pctCol"), filters a list of {field, values}. With several row fields, the PivotTable shows as a tree: subtotals places the group subtotals ("" on the group row, "bottom" below, "none" none); collapsed lists the collapsed groups, each by its labels ({"HR"}, {"HR", "Paris"}); collapseAll collapses everything except the groups in expanded. calc adds calculated fields, a list of {name, text}: text is a formula on the columns of each row of the source table ("=ANNEE([Date])", "=GAUCHE([Code];2)", formulas in French), and name the name of the field, which then goes into rowFields, cols, values or filters like a column (rows are grouped by its result). Parameters — config: configuration of the PivotTable. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

pivots.delete.details: Parameters — pivot: PivotTable (identifier or name). Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

pivots.set.summary: Replaces the configuration of a PivotTable.
pivots.set.details: config: {source, rowFields, cols, values, filters, calc, name, noGrandTotal, subtotals, collapsed, collapseAll, expanded}. source is a table, rowFields the list of row fields, cols the column field, values a list of {field, agg, show} (agg: "sum", "count", "countDistinct", "avg", "min" or "max"; show: "", "pctTotal", "pctRow" or "pctCol"), filters a list of {field, values}. With several row fields, the PivotTable shows as a tree: subtotals places the group subtotals ("" on the group row, "bottom" below, "none" none); collapsed lists the collapsed groups, each by its labels ({"HR"}, {"HR", "Paris"}); collapseAll collapses everything except the groups in expanded. calc adds calculated fields, a list of {name, text}: text is a formula on the columns of each row of the source table ("=ANNEE([Date])", "=GAUCHE([Code];2)", formulas in French), and name the name of the field, which then goes into rowFields, cols, values or filters like a column (rows are grouped by its result). Parameters — pivot: PivotTable (identifier or name); config: new configuration. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: pivots.set{pivot = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

queries.preview.details: Parameters — query: query (name or identifier); steps: number of steps applied. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: queries.preview{query = …}.

queries.refresh.details: Parameters — query: query (name or identifier). Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

queries.refresh_all.summary: Refreshes all the queries already loaded into a sheet.
queries.refresh_all.details: Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).

Parameters — name: name of the query; source: data source; steps: transformation steps. Arguments in order, or a table of named arguments: queries.save{name = …}. Undoable: everything the script changes is undone at once (Ctrl+Z).
